decisions.reason: The even-page rule is owned by the separate spread-compatibility Requirement; the requirement to deliver a digital flipbook remains unchanged.
The total-page-count rule does not change the free access tier or candidate flipbook platforms.
Requiring an even total page count does not change which cover-listed articles must be included or who decides their placement.
Pagination may be recalculated, but the cover's existing rule to display correct final page numbers remains valid unchanged.
The even-page rule is independent of the same-message request for future article word-count guidance.
The table of contents must still match finalized pagination; the even-page constraint does not alter that accuracy requirement.
An even total page count does not necessarily change the tribute page's required placement near the end of the magazine.
The source page-count decision does not change the article-end whitespace policy or its approved filler assets.
The flipbook's total page parity does not affect author names, photographs, sizing, sourcing, or placement.
The page-count constraint does not change the requirement to remediate article image quality when necessary.
The even-page rule does not change the magazine's polished, modern, brand-aligned visual style.
The general layout obligation and Flat Plan basis remain unchanged; copying the page-parity rule here would duplicate the atomic spread-compatibility Requirement.
